differences.title: 1. LANGUAGE SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi supports Python, TypeScript, Go, Java, C#, .NET, and YAML. Enables writing IaC in familiar languages with full SDK access and abstraction over providers.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK uses TypeScript, Python, Java, .NET, Go, or C++ for AWS-native IaC. Locks logic to AWS APIs with AWS construct libraries.

differences.title: 2. ABI
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi engine compiles to a single intermediate representation (Pulumi schema) that translates IaC to desired state across any provider. Avoids runtime interpretation.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK transforms high-level code into CloudFormation templates at synth-time. Templates are AWS-specific and evaluated by CloudFormation.

differences.title: 3. DEPENDENCY GRAPH
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi infers real dependencies between resources by analyzing reference edges in code, not order in file. Eliminates explicit dependency declarations.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK uses explicit `.addDependency()` calls or ordering in file to manage stack dependencies. Requires manual planning.

differences.title: 4. SDK INTEGRATION
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi integrates with any SDK or library in chosen language. Users call cloud providers’ official SDKs directly within IaC. Unrestricted extension.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK uses AWS Construct Library with limited abstractions. Some AWS features require raw CloudFormation or escape hatches.

differences.title: 5. STATE MANAGEMENT
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi stores state encrypted, supports self-hosted backends (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB), and offers full RBAC. No vendor lock-in for state lifecycle.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK uses CloudFormation to store state. State is AWS-owned, encrypted, and versioned, with limited RBAC outside AWS IAM.

differences.title: 6. EXTENSIONS & PLUGINS
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi supports dynamic providers via plugins (e.g., Kubernetes, Azure, GCP) and custom components. Community ecosystem thrives.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK extensions are limited to AWS Construct Hub or custom CDK constructs. Cross-cloud support requires third-party tools.

differences.title: 7. DEBUGGING & TESTING
differences.leftDesc: Pulumi supports `pulumi preview --diff` and `up --dry-run` for comprehensive state diffs. Integrates with IDE debugging for step-through IaC execution.
differences.rightDesc: AWS CDK uses `cdk diff` and `cdk deploy --no-execute-changeset` for preview. Debugging relies on CloudFormation drift detection.
